subject: ventures/rental-dscr-calculator
professional: a DSCR / investor-loan underwriter at a non-QM lender (with a rental-investment analyst's view of NOI, cap rate and IRR)

evidence.correctness: Recomputed the sample deal (350k, 25% down, 7.25%/30y, 2,900 rent, 5% vacancy, 8%+6% mgmt/maint, 4,200 tax, 1,800 ins) with an independent Python model (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/bfc40cd0-35aa-5329-b7a8-571e88aa5cb8/scratchpad/rental-dscr-calculator/indep.py, standard annuity and textbook NOI/DSCR definitions) and compared with `node -e analyze(sampleInput())`: payment 1,790.71 = 1,790.71; NOI 22,431.60 = 22,431.60; DSCR NOI 1.0439 = 1.0439; DSCR rent/PITIA 1.2660 = 1.2660; cap 6.409% and CoC 0.916% match; break-even occupancy 91.85% = 91.85%; max loan at 1.20 rent/PITIA 280,963.55 and NOI 228,350.07 match; 10-year IRR 10.2856% = 10.2856% (my own bisection). loanPayment(200000,6,30)=1,199.10 and loanPayment(100000,5,15)=790.79 match published amortization-table values. Every recomputed output matched. Gaps: break-even is clamped at 150% and printed as 'about 150%' (rent 1,200 case: true value (6000+21488.55)/(14400*0.86)=222%), and the max loan has no LTV/price cap (rent 6,000 gives a 'largest loan' of $659,654 on a $350,000 house).
evidence.completeness: Ran `node --test '*.test.mjs'`: 37/37 pass. Checked every README/page feature via analyze(): DSCR both ways, cash-on-cash, cap rate, break-even, max loan both definitions, interest-only (finding shown, balance held), rate table -1..+3 points, 10-40 year hold table with sale and IRR, CSV export (formula-neutralised), opt-out local usage counts honouring DNT (usage.test.mjs). served-copy.mjs reports no placeholder origin. All work; no stubs or TODOs found.
evidence.verification: 37 tests pass, and they pin payment, NOI, both DSCRs and CoC to hand values. But 4 of 5 non-equivalent seeded mutants in core logic survived via quality_mutate.py: break-even dropping maintenance (calc.mjs:73), max-loan dropping HOA (calc.mjs:163), hold table dropping vacancy (calc.mjs:82), lender DSCR dropping other income (calc.mjs:69). Only opex-on-gross (calc.mjs:60) was caught. A fifth candidate (sale balance months) was equivalent because balanceAfter clamps at zero, so it is not counted.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (187 lines), index.html script, usage.mjs. Compact, pure, exported functions; CSV injection guarded; parseNum strict but strips commas correctly ('1,200,000' -> 1200000, run). Defects: termYears '0' passes validation (message says 0 to 40 allowed) and is silently replaced by 30 (`Math.round(o.termYears) || 30`, calc.mjs:140, run: term0 -> 30); unreachable check at calc.mjs:135 (downPct capped at 100 already); rate table repeats the literal [-1,0,1,2,3] four times in one line (calc.mjs:158) and clamps a -1 point row at 0% while still labelling it '-1 point' (run with apr 0.5); break-even clamp hides the real value.
evidence.claims: Disclaimer (no warranty, not advice, verify) is on index.html:151 and README; 'Unverified: checked by hand calculation and unit tests only' is honest; not-modelled list is explicit. Privacy claim backed: grep finds no fetch/sendBeacon/XMLHttpRequest; page.test asserts no network; DNT honoured (usage.mjs:34). Formula claims on the page match the code (rerun above). Weak spots: page and README say 'the largest loan your lender's minimum allows' though it can exceed the price (no LTV cap), and 'scheduled gross rent' in the lender-style ratio actually includes other income (calc.mjs:69).
evidence.fitness: Walked an investor's job: enter a deal, read whether it clears 1.20, see the max loan and rate risk, export the year table. Works in seconds on the sample and on a weak deal (rent 1,200: flagged below target and negative cash flow). Enough for a pre-offer screen; an underwriter's real sizing (lesser of lease and 1007 market rent, LTV cap, IO qualifying rules) still has to be done by hand.
evidence.domain: Against DSCR-lender practice (gross monthly rent over PITIA, with rent the lesser of lease and appraiser's Form 1007 market rent; LTV caps around 75-80% on purchases; HOA in PITIA; vacancy not deducted) the tool gets PITIA, HOA and gross-not-net right, and qualifies IO loans on the IO payment, which many lenders do. Departs in two places: adds 'other income' to the lender-style numerator (other income 500/month moves DSCR 1.266 -> 1.484, run), and sizes the max loan on coverage alone with no LTV cap. The NOI side (management and maintenance on EGI, cap rate on price) is standard analyst practice.

defects.what: Largest loan at the target DSCR is sized on coverage alone, with no LTV or price cap: rent 6,000 on a 350,000 house reports a 659,654 'largest loan your lender's minimum allows'. DSCR lenders cap purchase LTV (commonly 75-80%).

Lender-style DSCR (rent / PITIA) adds other income to the numerator, though the page calls it scheduled gross rent and DSCR lenders use rent alone (lesser of lease and Form 1007 market rent); 500/month other income lifts 1.266 to 1.484 and also inflates maxLoanRent (line 162).

4 of 5 seeded core mutants survive: break-even without maintenance, max loan without HOA, hold table without vacancy, lender DSCR without other income. The break-even test sets maintenance to 0 and no test pins hold-year NOI with vacancy or maxLoanRent with HOA.
Break-even occupancy is clamped at 150% and shown as 'about 150%' (true 222% for rent 1,200); a capped value should read '150% or more'.
Loan term '0' passes validation (the error text says 0 to 40 is allowed) and is silently replaced by 30 years.
Unreachable down-payment check (downPct is already capped at 100) and the rate-shift array literal repeated four times; at a rate under 1% the '-1 point' row is clamped to 0% but keeps its label.

verdict: A tidy, honest DSCR screen whose arithmetic is right. Against an independent Python model and published amortization values, every recomputed output for the sample deal matches to the cent: payment 1,790.71, NOI 22,431.60, DSCR 1.2660 rent/PITIA and 1.0439 NOI, break-even 91.85%, max loans 280,963.55 and 228,350.07, and 10-year IRR 10.2856%. Disclaimer, a not-modelled list and an 'unverified' line are on the page, and the no-upload claim holds. A DSCR underwriter would object in two places: the lender-style ratio counts other income as rent, and the 'largest loan' has no LTV cap, so it can exceed the price (659,654 on a 350,000 house). Break-even is clamped at 150% and shown as if exact. The 37 tests pass but miss 4 of 5 seeded core mutants. Does not meet the bar: verification is 1, and correctness 3, claims 3, median 3. Finished (completeness 3). Fixable in one session: use rent only in the lender ratio (or a separate rent field), cap the max loan at price times an LTV input, print '150%+' for a clamped break-even, reject a zero term, and add tests that pin vacancy, HOA and maintenance in the outputs they feed.
